conventions.convention: Assume full AC; use the standard finite product torus T = (R/Z)^r, including the one-point group when r = 0.
The coordinate tangent basis has period one: exp_T(s e_i) has coordinate [s] in position i. Quotient interval charts determine the smooth structure.

ET is the finite product of the chosen right Milnor circle models, and BT is its ordinary orbit quotient. The real generator u_i is pulled back from the complex-oriented tautological-line Euler class, with e_i* mapped to u_i.
The Borel quotient uses the right action (e,p)·t = (e·t,t⁻¹·p); Borel equivariant cohomology means real singular cohomology of that quotient.

M is a smooth manifold without boundary with a jointly smooth left torus action; compactness of M is not assumed. Cartan tensor products are algebraic, polynomial linear generators have degree two, and the polynomial torus action is trivial.
Fundamental fields use exp_T(−sξ); the Cartan differential is d_T = d − Σu_i ι_Xei. No general Borel–Cartan comparison is asserted.
For the translation circle example, X_e = −∂x and η descends from −dx, so contraction is ι_Xeη = 1 and d_Tη = −u.

load_bearing.statement: For a smooth left action of the standard product torus on a boundaryless smooth manifold M, Borel equivariant cohomology is H_sing*(ET ×_T M; R). The Cartan complex is (Sym_R(t*) ⊗_R Ω*(M))^T with polynomial generators in degree two and differential d_T(P ⊗ α) = P ⊗ dα − Σ(u_iP) ⊗ ι_Xeiα. Its square is zero on invariant elements. No general isomorphism between these two cohomology rings is asserted.

Assume AC. For T = (R/Z)^r with its fixed product decomposition and ET the product of the right Milnor circle models, BT is homeomorphic to (CP∞)^r and H*(BT; R) is R[u_1,…,u_r], with |u_i| = 2. Each u_i is the pullback of the real coefficient image of the complex-oriented tautological-line Euler class. Sending e_i* to u_i identifies Sym_R(t*) with this graded ring. For r = 0 both rings are R.

Assume full AC. Give T = (R/Z)^r the quotient circle charts and product smooth structure, with period-one coordinate tangent basis and exp_T(s e_i) equal to the corresponding coordinate subgroup. For r = 0 use the one-point group and empty basis. T is a compact connected abelian Lie group and its identity inclusion is a cofibration, so it is well-pointed.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.1 says that for M empty, “both the form complex and the Borel construction are empty.” The Borel space is empty, but the form complex is the zero complex: each space of sections contains its unique zero section. The resulting zero-cohomology conclusion is correct; the description of the complex should say zero rather than empty.

seams_checked.note: The rigid-background postulate F2 uses only the finite-dimensional smooth Cartan complex and explicitly excludes an inferred identification with an infinite-dimensional field-space complex.

The round-S4 example F2 and Verification 4.1 apply the definition to the smooth circle action on the boundaryless finite-dimensional base S4, while retaining the separation from field configuration space and formal measure assumptions.

Character localization preserves the product Milnor model and diagonal quotient. Its rational coefficients and character-line formulas receive separate support from the rational classifying-space lemma; that lemma identifies the weight-one associated line with the tautological line, matching the owned real generator normalization.

The three examples use Borel cohomology and the same character classes. The free-orbit quotient map agrees with the owned free-circle computation. Rational coefficients and fixed-component product calculations use separate localization suppliers; no general Cartan comparison is imported.

The integration conventions retain the period-one basis, real coefficient ring, tautological Euler generators and equivalent relation (e·t,x) ∼ (e,t·x). The additional pushforward and Thom constructions are separately supplied, and the text explicitly avoids assuming a Cartan comparison. The owned associated-space square has correctly directed arrows and commutes by projection.
